proof.text: Use the coherent nerve and functor conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the cocartesian convention of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. In the definition of a symmetric monoidal infinity category in the statement, the fiber equivalences are induced by precisely the maps $\rho_i$. Thus the only condition imposed on a cocartesian fibration over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$, besides being a cocartesian fibration, is that these fiber maps be equivalences, also for the empty family.

source.place: Definitions 2.0.0.7 and 2.4.2.1; Remark 2.1.2.19 (the condition being compared is explicitly defined in the item)

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] with $S=N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$. For every $i$, its identification of fibers and transport identifies pushforward along $\rho_i$ with $F(\rho_i)$. Consequently the fiber equivalence of step 1 is exactly the displayed Segal equivalence. Restrict the general straightening equivalence to the full subcategories of objects satisfying these conditions. Its inverse restricts as well: unstraightening such an $F$ has fibers $F(\langle n\rangle)$ and the prescribed transport, hence satisfies step 1. When $n=0$, the product is terminal and the condition is $F(\langle0\rangle)\simeq *$; when $n=1$, $\rho_1$ is the identity.

Write $\mu_n:\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ for the map sending each non-basepoint to $1$, and use $F(\mu_n)$ after the Segal equivalence as the tensor. For $n=0$ this is a functor from a terminal category selecting the unit; for $n=1$ it is the identity. For a general pointed map $\alpha$, the identity $\rho_j\alpha=\mu_{|\alpha^{-1}(j)|}\pi_j$, where $\pi_j$ selects that block, identifies its $j$th output with the tensor of the inputs in that block. Composing pointed maps composes these partitions, so the image under $F$ of each composable string supplies its associativity comparison. Identity maps supply unit comparisons and permutations supply symmetry comparisons. The higher simplices for these strings and their faces give their compatibility, since they are images under a single functor $F$. This describes the coherences, rather than imposing equations on tensor operations alone.

The definition of the infinity category $\operatorname{coCart}(S)$ in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], with the core convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], identifies its mapping spaces with the cores of the strong-functor subcategories. Its straightening equivalence therefore identifies the space of natural transformations $F_{\mathcal A}\to F_{\mathcal B}$ with the core of the full subcategory of functors over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ preserving cocartesian edges. By the definition in the item these are exactly strong symmetric monoidal functors. Restricting to Segal objects changes neither mapping space. Thus the correspondence includes natural equivalences between those strong functors and every higher homotopy. This assertion concerns the mapping spaces of the classification; the full infinity category $\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}$ used next also keeps noninvertible monoidal transformations.

source.place: Definition 2.1.3.7 and Remark 2.4.2.6, together with general straightening

proof.text: We will use the following elementary pullback check. For a cocartesian fibration $q:E\to B$ and $a:T\to B$ with $T$ a quasicategory, the degreewise pullback $q_T:T\times_B E\to T$ is an inner fibration, because each inner-horn problem is a problem for $q$ with its $T$-coordinate fixed. The same argument with the outer horns in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] shows that every $q$-cocartesian lift pulls back to a $q_T$-cocartesian lift; these provide lifts for every base edge. Conversely, let $v:x\to y$ be $q_T$-cocartesian over $\alpha:t\to t\prime$, and choose a $q$-cocartesian lift $w:x\to y\prime$ of $a(\alpha)$. The $K=\Delta^0$ mapping-space fiber formula of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] factors the image of $v$ as $h w$, with $h:y\prime\to y$ in the common target fiber. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], applied to the inner fibration $q_T$ between quasicategories, $v$ and the pulled-back $w$ satisfy the homotopy-pullback mapping squares of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]; restricted to that fiber, they says that precomposition by $h$ induces equivalences $\operatorname{Map}(y,z)\to\operatorname{Map}(y\prime,z)$ for every $z$ in the fiber. At $z=y\prime$ this gives $g:y\to y\prime$ with $gh\simeq\mathrm{id}$; injectivity on components at $z=y$ then gives $hg\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Hence $h$ is an equivalence. Precomposition with an equivalence preserves the homotopy-pullback mapping square for $w$, so $h w$, the image of $v$, satisfies it, and the converse direction of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] for $q$ shows that it is $q$-cocartesian. Thus an edge of the pullback is cocartesian exactly when its $E$-component is. This proves the edge criterion here rather than attributing it to a clause absent from the current straightening node.

source.place: Dual Proposition 2.4.2.3(2) and Remark 2.4.2.13; explicit horn and fiber-universal-property argument from the cited statements.

proof.text: Set $S=N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and, using [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to identify its horn-cocartesian edges with the mapping-square cocartesian edges, apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to $p:\mathcal B^\otimes\to S$. The pullback clause of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], applied along the constant-diagram map $S\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,S)$, identifies the classifying diagram of the pullback $D_K\to S$. The horn and edge check in step 5 gives its cocartesian fibration structure and detects its cocartesian edges in the functor category. Combined with the vertex criterion, these are exactly the pointwise cocartesian edges. This pullback has fiber $\operatorname{Fun}(K,F_{\mathcal B}(\langle n\rangle))$ and transport obtained by postcomposing with that of $\mathcal B^\otimes$. Hence straightening identifies its diagram with the one in the statement. Its transport is obtained by taking the pointwise lifts supplied by that theorem, now lying over a constant-base transformation. The Segal equivalences follow because taking simplicial maps from $K\times\Delta^r$ commutes with products in every degree, so $\operatorname{Fun}(K,F_{\mathcal B}(\langle1\rangle)^n)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,F_{\mathcal B}(\langle1\rangle))^n$. The functor-category theorem [lem-coef-infinity-functor-pushout] ensures these internal Homs are quasicategories and preserve equivalences. Its underlying category is $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)$, and its tensors and unit are evaluated at each vertex, by the pointwise transport description.

Simplicial currying gives an isomorphism between functors $\mathcal A^\otimes\to D_K$ over $S$ and functors $K\to\operatorname{Fun}_S(\mathcal A^\otimes,\mathcal B^\otimes)$. Explicitly an $r$-simplex on either side is a map $K\times\mathcal A^\otimes\times\Delta^r\to\mathcal B^\otimes$ whose composite with $p$ is the projection through $\mathcal A^\otimes\to S$. These identifications commute with every face and degeneracy. By the pullback edge criterion proved in step 5 from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] and [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] and the vertex criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], a vertex on the left preserves cocartesian edges exactly when each vertex $k$ of $K$ gives a cocartesian-edge-preserving functor on the right. A full subcategory contains exactly simplices whose vertices belong to it, so the isomorphism restricts to the two full subcategories displayed in the statement, including their noninvertible transformations. Permuting the $K$ and $\mathcal A^\otimes$ factors and evaluating proves naturality in $K$, $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Remark 2.1.3.4 and Definition 2.1.3.7; explicit restriction of simplicial currying

proof.text: For an ordinary symmetric monoidal $A$, use its operadic category $A^\otimes$: objects are finite tuples and the arrows over $\alpha$ are the block maps in the statement. Its composition sends block maps $f_j$ over $\alpha$ and $g_k$ over $\beta$ to $g_k\circ(\bigotimes_{\beta(j)=k}f_j)$ after the structural regrouping $\bigotimes_{\beta\alpha(i)=k}X_i\cong\bigotimes_{\beta(j)=k}(\bigotimes_{\alpha(i)=j}X_i)$. For a tuple $X$ and $\alpha$, put $Y_j=\bigotimes_{\alpha(i)=j}X_i$ and take all block maps to be identities. For every subsequent pointed map $\beta$ and target tuple $Z$, precomposition with this arrow is a bijection on arrows over $\beta$ onto arrows from $X$ over $\beta\alpha$: both consist of the maps $\bigotimes_{\beta\alpha(i)=k}X_i\to Z_k$, using exactly the displayed regrouping. A nerve simplex is a string of composable arrows, so an inner horn already determines the missing composite; hence the nerve of any ordinary functor is an inner fibration. Its mapping spaces are the discrete Hom sets: in the right-pinched model every initial vertex is fixed and the remaining edge must be the same in every face. Thus the preceding Hom-set bijection is precisely the homotopy cartesian mapping square defining a cocartesian edge in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]; by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] for this inner fibration of quasicategories, the identity block map is a horn-cocartesian lift in $N(A^\otimes)$. The fiber over $\langle n\rangle$ is $N(A^n)$, which is $N(A)^n$ because a chain in a product category is a tuple of chains. Inert projections select the individual objects. The empty tuple is the unique object and arrow of the zero fiber; empty blocks give the tensor unit. Hence these fibers satisfy the Segal condition, and the fiber over $\langle1\rangle$ is $N(A)$.

title: Symmetric monoidal infinity categories as Segal diagrams
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], enlarging universes as necessary. Let $\mathsf{Fin}_*$ be the category of finite pointed sets, write $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\rho_i:\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ send $i$ to $1$ and every other element to $*$. An inert map has exactly one preimage for each non-basepoint of its target. A Segal diagram is a functor $F:N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)\to\mathsf{Cat}_\infty$ for which $(F(\rho_i))_i:F(\langle n\rangle)\to F(\langle1\rangle)^n$ is an equivalence for every $n\geq0$, including $F(\langle0\rangle)\simeq *$. Here $N$ denotes the simplicial nerve. A symmetric monoidal infinity category is encoded by a cocartesian fibration $p:\mathcal A^{\otimes}\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ whose fiber over $\langle n\rangle$ is identified with $\mathcal A^n$, $\mathcal A=p^{-1}(\langle1\rangle)$, by pushforward along the $\rho_i$. Straightening, which assigns to a cocartesian fibration its fibers and pushforward functors, identifies symmetric monoidal infinity categories with Segal diagrams: the inverse, unstraightening, produces a cocartesian fibration over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ with those fibers. The underlying category is $F(\langle1\rangle)$; the active maps $\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ sending all non-basepoints to $1$ give its $n$-ary tensor operations, including the unit when $n=0$. Natural transformations between Segal diagrams correspond to strong symmetric monoidal functors, meaning functors over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ preserving cocartesian arrows, and this correspondence identifies their spaces of equivalences and higher homotopies.

For symmetric monoidal $\mathcal A^{\otimes},\mathcal B^{\otimes}$, let $\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ be the full infinity subcategory of functors between their total categories over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ spanned by these strong functors; its morphisms are monoidal natural transformations, not necessarily invertible. For every small infinity category $K$, the functor category $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)$ has the pointwise symmetric monoidal structure, classified by $\langle n\rangle\mapsto\operatorname{Fun}(K,F_{\mathcal B}(\langle n\rangle))$, and currying gives a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal A,\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B))\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)).$$
For an ordinary symmetric monoidal category $A$, its operadic nerve $N(A^{\otimes})$ is such a symmetric monoidal infinity category, with underlying category $N(A)$. Here objects of $A^{\otimes}$ are finite tuples, and a morphism over $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$ consists of maps $\bigotimes_{\alpha(i)=j}X_i\to Y_j$ for $1\leq j\leq m$.
